name: Nginx Webhost
author: mohamed@rustix.xyz
description:
Host any PHP or static website with nginx + PHP-FPM.

- Composer: list packages in "Composer modules" and they're installed on startup
- WordPress: turn on the WordPress option when creating the server
- Git: clone your site from a Git repo, optionally pulling updates on every start
- Mail, Site, Discord, Google and database variables are passed to PHP, so sites read them with getenv() instead of hardcoding them

Based on the WebHost egg by Sigma Productions (originally tenten8401/pterodactyl-nginx).

installation.script: #!/bin/ash # Nginx Webhost installer: installs the nginx/PHP config and sets up the website files. # Bump this whenever the egg or the repo's config files change. Servers compare it with # the egg on GitHub at startup and show an update notice in the console. EGG_VERSION="1.0.5" REPO="https://github.com/Rustix-Development/pterodactyl-nginx-egg" is_true() { [ "$1" = "1" ] || [ "$1" = "true" ]; } # Drop user:token@ from a git URL so a changed token still counts as the same repo strip_auth() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed -E 's#^([a-z]+://)[^/@]*@#\1#'; } trap 'rm -rf /tmp/egg' EXIT # The install container has a terminal nobody types into: never wait for a git password export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 cd /mnt/server || exit 1 apk add --no-cache git curl || { echo "Failed to install git and curl"; exit 1; } # Server files belong to the server user, not root; let git work on them anyway git config --global --add safe.directory '*' echo "Downloading config files from ${REPO}" rm -rf /tmp/egg git clone --depth 1 "${REPO}" /tmp/egg || { echo "Failed to download config files"; exit 1; } if [ ! -f /tmp/egg/start.sh ] || [ ! -d /tmp/egg/nginx ] || [ ! -d /tmp/egg/php-fpm ]; then echo "Config files are missing from ${REPO} (empty repo or wrong default branch?)" exit 1 fi # Config files are replaced on every (re)install cp -r /tmp/egg/nginx /tmp/egg/php-fpm /mnt/server/ \ && cp /tmp/egg/start.sh /mnt/server/start.sh \ && chmod +x /mnt/server/start.sh \ || { echo "Failed to copy config files"; exit 1; } # Left behind by older versions of this egg, it stops nginx from starting rm -f /mnt/server/nginx/conf.d/nextcloud.conf mkdir -p /mnt/server/webroot /mnt/server/tmp /mnt/server/logs echo "${EGG_VERSION}" > /mnt/server/.egg-version echo "Installed Nginx Webhost egg v${EGG_VERSION} config files" cd /mnt/server/webroot || exit 1 # A default landing page (this egg's or an older egg's) doesn't count as a website if [ "$(ls -A)" = "index.php" ] && grep -qE 'Web server is running|Webserver Correctly Installed' index.php; then rm -f index.php fi seed_default_page() { if [ -z "$(ls -A)" ]; then cp /tmp/egg/webroot/index.php ./ fi } # WordPress if is_true "${WORDPRESS}"; then if [ -f wp-load.php ]; then echo "WordPress is already installed, leaving it alone." elif [ -n "$(ls -A)" ]; then echo "webroot already has files, not installing WordPress over them." else echo "Installing WordPress..." # Unpack outside webroot so a broken download never leaves files behind in it WP_TMP=/mnt/server/.wordpress-download rm -rf "${WP_TMP}" && mkdir -p "${WP_TMP}" if ! curl -fsSL https://wordpress.org/latest.tar.gz | tar xz -C "${WP_TMP}" || [ ! -f "${WP_TMP}/wordpress/wp-load.php" ]; then rm -rf "${WP_TMP}" echo "Failed to download WordPress" exit 1 fi cp -a "${WP_TMP}/wordpress/." . && rm -rf "${WP_TMP}" echo "WordPress installed. Finish setup at http://ip:port/wp-admin" fi exit 0 fi if is_true "${USER_UPLOAD}"; then seed_default_page echo "User Uploaded Files is on, skipping website setup. Upload your files into webroot." exit 0 fi if [ -z "${GIT_ADDRESS}" ]; then seed_default_page echo "Install complete. No Git Repo Address set, upload your website into webroot." exit 0 fi # Git case "${GIT_ADDRESS}" in *.git) ;; *) GIT_ADDRESS="${GIT_ADDRESS}.git" ;; esac if [ -n "${USERNAME}" ] && [ -n "${ACCESS_TOKEN}" ]; then GIT_ADDRESS="https://${USERNAME}:${ACCESS_TOKEN}@${GIT_ADDRESS#*://}" fi if [ -n "$(ls -A)" ]; then if [ -d .git ]; then if [ "$(strip_auth "$(git config --get remote.origin.url)")" = "$(strip_auth "${GIT_ADDRESS}")" ]; then echo "Pulling latest website files from git" # Picks up a changed Git Username/Access Token git remote set-url origin "${GIT_ADDRESS}" git pull --ff-only || echo "git pull failed, keeping the current files." else echo "webroot is a clone of a different git repo, leaving it alone." fi else echo "webroot already has files that aren't from git, leaving them alone." fi else echo "Cloning website files from git" if [ -n "${BRANCH}" ]; then git clone --single-branch --branch "${BRANCH}" "${GIT_ADDRESS}" . || { echo "git clone failed, check Git Repo Address, Git Branch and credentials"; exit 1; } else git clone "${GIT_ADDRESS}" . || { echo "git clone failed, check Git Repo Address and credentials"; exit 1; } fi fi echo "Install complete. Visit http://ip:port/"

variables.name: Startup Command
variables.description:
The command to startup the egg 
(Do not change if you do not know what you are doing!)

variables.name: Wordpress
variables.description:
Enable or disable Wordpress

0 = false (default)
1 = true

variables.name: Composer modules
variables.description:
Composer packages to install into webroot, separated by spaces, e.g. "phpmailer/phpmailer vlucas/phpdotenv". Pin a version with vendor/package:^6.0.

Each package is added once and then kept at that version; on every start the server runs composer install so vendor/ matches composer.lock.

variables.name: Git Repo Address
variables.description:
Git repo to clone your website from.

I.E. https://github.com/your-name/your-site

Leave blank to upload files yourself.

variables.name: Git Branch
variables.description:
What branch to pull from github.

Default is blank to pull the repo default branch

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description:
Pull the latest files from the Git repo on every start.

0 = false (default)
1 = true

variables.name: User Uploaded Files
variables.description:
Skip all the install stuff if you are letting a user upload files.

0 = false (default)
1 = true

variables.name: Root Folder
variables.description:
Folder inside webroot to serve at your domain's root, a name or a path: <folder> serves webroot/<folder> at /, dev/main serves webroot/dev/main. The other folders in webroot are still served at their own path (webroot/blog at /blog/), and links to /<folder>/... redirect to /...

Leave blank to serve webroot as is (default).

variables.name: 404 Page
variables.description:
Page to show when a page doesn't exist, e.g. 404.html or errors/404.php (HTML or PHP), from your site's root (webroot, or the Root Folder if set). Visitors get it with a 404 status.

Leave blank to send missing pages to index.php as before (default, needed for WordPress and other apps that show their own 404).

variables.name: Update Check
variables.description:
Check GitHub on startup and say in the console when the egg or the Docker image has an update.

0 = false
1 = true (default)

variables.name: Git Username
variables.description: Username to auth with git.

variables.name: Git Access Token
variables.description:
Password to use with git.

It's best practice to use a Personal Access Token.
https://github.com/settings/tokens
https://gitlab.com/-/profile/personal_access_tokens

variables.name: SMTP Host
variables.description:
SMTP server address used to send mail from this site.

Default works for Resend (recommended — works from any IP, no dedicated mailbox needed). Set to smtp.gmail.com for Gmail / Google Workspace instead.

variables.name: SMTP Port
variables.description: SMTP port. 465 (implicit TLS) is correct for Resend. Use 587 (STARTTLS) for Gmail / Google Workspace.

variables.name: SMTP Username
variables.description:
The account that sends the mail.

For Resend this is always literally "resend" (not an email address). For Gmail/Workspace this is the full mailbox address, e.g. info@yoursite.com.

variables.name: SMTP Password
variables.description:
For Resend: your Resend API key (starts with "re_").

For Gmail / Google Workspace: an App Password for the mailbox above, no spaces — requires 2-Step Verification first: https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords. Never a normal account password.

variables.name: Mail From Email
variables.description: The address mail appears to come FROM, e.g. noreply@yoursite.com. Required for Resend (must be on a domain you've verified with them). For Gmail/Workspace, leave blank to default to SMTP Username.

variables.name: Mail From Name
variables.description:
The display name shown as the sender on outgoing mail, e.g. "My Site".

Leave blank to fall back to "{Site Name} Contact Form".

variables.name: Mail To Email
variables.description: Where contact form submissions actually land, usually the office inbox for this site.

variables.name: Site Name
variables.description:
Short name for this site, used in the contact form's email subject line and internal error logs, e.g. "My Site".

Purely cosmetic, doesn't need to match anything else.

variables.name: Site URL
variables.description:
The public URL this site is reached at, no trailing slash, e.g. "https://example.com".

Used to build password reset links, unsubscribe links, email notification links, and the Discord OAuth redirect URL. Leave blank to fall back to the value baked into config.php.

variables.name: Discord Client ID
variables.description:
OAuth2 Client ID from your app at https://discord.com/developers/applications.

Leave both this and Discord Client Secret blank to keep Discord login disabled.

variables.name: Discord Client Secret
variables.description:
OAuth2 Client Secret from the same Discord application (OAuth2 tab). Treat this like a password.

After setting this, add this EXACT redirect URL in that app's OAuth2 settings: {Site URL}/discord-callback/

variables.name: Database Connection String
variables.description: Paste your database connection string here — same format the panel's own DB_CONNECTION_STRING auto-injects (e.g. "jdbc:mysql://user:pass@host:port/dbname"), or a plain "mysql://user:pass@host:port/dbname", or a PDO-style "mysql:host=X;port=Y;dbname=Z;user=U;password=P". Leave blank to rely on the panel's automatic database attachment instead.

variables.name: Google Client ID
variables.description:
OAuth2 Client ID from a Web application client at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials.

Leave both this and Google Client Secret blank to keep Google login disabled. Unlike Discord, Google sign-in never creates a new account — it only works for someone whose Google email already matches an existing staff account.

variables.name: Google Client Secret
variables.description:
OAuth2 Client Secret from the same Google Cloud OAuth client. Treat this like a password.

After setting this, add this EXACT redirect URL as an "Authorized redirect URI" on that client: {Site URL}/google-callback/
